extracted.intended_audience: UCI faculty, researchers, and research administrators seeking grant funding and institutional proposal support
extracted.subtask_description: Information on UCI's Research Development services and the different types of funding (external, limited, internal), plus who to contact and how proposals are supported. Focused on helping faculty find opportunities and develop competitive proposals, especially for large or interdisciplinary projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Development team focus / prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Development team is charged with advancing and supporting sponsored research across all of UCI and is especially focused on large or complex, interdisciplinary projects that involve multiple faculty, departments or research units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The team prioritizes multi‑faculty, multi‑department, interdisciplinary, large or complex projects. They work with and support school Research Development Officers (RDOs) to assist faculty on such proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of Research Development Officers (RDOs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Development Officers across campus work with faculty to help with funding searches, provide grantsmanship advice and provide other support in proposal development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty should contact the RDO in their School to set up a meeting for help with funding strategy and proposal development; if a School lacks an RDO, contact the Director of Research Development (Michael Gallo). RDOs' role is hands‑on support to develop 'winning grant proposals.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying funding opportunities (use of curated search tools)
rubrics_metrics.description: The office has gathered a curated list of funding search tools that cover the gamut of research sponsors: government, non‑profit, corporate and international.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided curated search tools to find appropriate sponsors. The list is intended to help faculty scan the full range of possible funders; links to the search tools are provided on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with Corporate and Foundation Relations for non‑federal funding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Development team works closely with the Corporate and Foundation Relations team in UCI Advancement which provides support for non‑federal funding program opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For corporate or foundation (non‑federal) opportunities, engage both Research Development and Advancement's Corporate & Foundation Relations to leverage complementary expertise and institutional relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of External Funding Opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: External Funding Opportunities refer to any research sponsor (such as the federal government, non‑profit organizations, and corporations) — i.e., funding coming from and applications submitted outside of UCI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The office provides a non‑exhaustive list of external sponsors with brief notes on what kinds of projects they fund and links to a dedicated External Funding page for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited Funding Opportunities: internal selection requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited opportunities are externally sponsored grants that require an internal selection process, usually because the sponsor limits the number of applications that can be submitted by UCI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested applicants must submit a pre‑proposal to the Office of Research (unless otherwise indicated). A committee reviews submissions and makes a recommendation to the Vice Chancellor for Research about which proposal should be submitted from UCI. Limited opportunities are advertised on fundopp.uci.edu (along with internal competitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Funding Opportunities: typical one‑stage internal awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal Funding Opportunities are grants internal to UCI offered by a UCI unit to UCI personnel; selection processes vary by unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically internal competitions are a one‑stage process where selected applicants are awarded funding directly by the entity managing the competition. The office maintains a non‑exhaustive list of recurring internal opportunities to illustrate available internal funding types.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to request RD support / contact procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty needing proposal development help should contact their School RDO or the Director of Research Development if their School lacks an RDO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical contact information is provided (Director Michael A. Gallo Jr., email and phone). Use the 'Find Your RDO' resource to locate school‑specific support and set up meetings for strategy and proposal development assistance.
